findings.finding: Parent AC6 requires the parametrized characterization suite to contain at least one case for EACH of TWO specifically named divergences — '(a) rich text, ADF vs wiki markup' and '(b) identity form, Cloud `accountId` vs DC `name`' — in which Cloud and DC parameters carry DIFFERENT expected values, and BOTH cases pass. Child `cedc` AC7 states only the generic negative constraint: 'no assertion claims parity where the adapters correctly diverge.' This does not satisfy the three-part coverage standard: (1) the observable outcome is different (a positive enumeration of two named cases vs. a negative absence-of-parity-claims constraint); (2) the scope is narrower (the child's AC does not require cases for both (a) and (b)); (3) it is not measurable in the same terms (a completion verifier of cedc alone cannot confirm both named divergences have dedicated parametrized cases).
scenarios: An implementer reading only cedc's ACs writes a parametrized suite that covers identity form (b) with different Cloud/DC values but omits a paired rich-text (a) case with different values; cedc's ACs are all satisfied but parent AC6 is not

findings.finding: Epic-level AC6 requires 'the parametrized characterization suite must contain at least one case for EACH known divergence,' but `cedc`'s own plan explicitly allows a separate DC file as a valid fallback ('a split is the fallback, not the default'). If the implementer takes the split path, AC6's 'parametrized characterization suite' language becomes ambiguous: it is unclear whether two separate files (one Cloud, one DC) jointly satisfy AC6, or whether AC6 requires a SINGLE parametrized file. An implementer or reviewer who reads AC6 literally would reject a valid split-file implementation; one who reads `cedc` loosely might produce a parametrized file that obscures Cloud's incident-hardened pins. The two specs are in genuine tension and the resolution is not stated in the plan.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace AC6's 'the parametrized characterization suite' with 'the characterization suite (whether parametrized or split per cedc's scope)' so the criterion is verifiable under either implementation strategy.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` consumer inventory by running `find_referencing_symbols` on the symbol in addition to the existing string grep, and separately grep for the post-relocation canonical name (`LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` or whichever alias is chosen) to surface any references to the new name that the old-name grep cannot find.
evidence: bd9e description: 'A repo-wide git grep -n _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE (string grep, not just a semantic reference search — the LSP does not see string/attribute access reliably) returns exactly seven sites'

The plan correctly notes LSP misses string/attribute access and supplements with grep, but does NOT also run find_referencing_symbols on _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE to get structural references — only grep was used, as stated.

After relocation the canonical name changes to LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA (or similar); a grep for the OLD private name finds sites that need the alias, but a grep for the NEW public name is needed to ensure no site references it under the new name in a way the alias strategy does not cover. The plan documents no such forward-looking sweep.
findings.finding: The bd9e child ticket's consumer enumeration for `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` is explicitly stated to have been produced by `git grep` rather than by symbol-graph lookup (`find_referencing_symbols`) plus a separate string sweep. Per the rubric's stated-method branch, a plan that positively says it grepped its way to an inventory is a finding on that statement alone, because grep misses dynamic dispatch, `monkeypatch.setattr`, `importlib.import_module`, string-based parametrize tables, and attribute-access references that appear as string literals. Although the result is factually complete in this case (my search corroborates all 7 sites), a complete result from an unsound method is luck, not evidence, and the same method applied to the new name (`LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA` in `value_maps.py`) after relocation must not rely on luck.
findings.location: bd9e child ticket description, section 'Every consumer of the symbol, enumerated': "A repo-wide git grep -n _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE (string grep, not just a semantic reference search — the LSP does not see string/attribute access reliably) returns exactly seven sites, and the plan accounts for all of them"
scenarios: If any test or module references `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE` via `getattr(module, '_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE')` or via `monkeypatch.setattr(..., '_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE', ...)` rather than a direct import, grep finds it but find_referencing_symbols would not — the rubric requires both sweeps, and only grep was run here.

After relocation, the new canonical name (e.g. `LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA`) may be referenced in places the old-name grep did not surface; without a symbol-graph sweep of the new name, those sites are invisible to the plan's inventory.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `find_referencing_symbols('_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE')` to get structural references, keep the string grep for dynamic/string-based uses, then after choosing the canonical name run a string grep for that new name across the full repo to catch any forward references.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve ownership of DC create-path issuetype pins: either cedc AC1 is narrowed to exclude `issuetype` (deferring to bd9e) with an explicit 'reuse bd9e's pins' clause, or bd9e's ownership claim is removed and cedc owns all characterization pins — one child, one deliverable, no overlap.

bd9e body (Testing section): 'Ownership note: sibling story cedc (DC backend characterization suite) also touches DC create-path characterization. To remove the ambiguity, the type-mapping pins are owned here; cedc depends on this ticket and should reuse these pins rather than re-author them.'
cedc AC1: 'the create-path mapper _map_local_to_dc_fields is pinned by VALUE for every key it emits — summary, description, issuetype, priority, status, assignee'
cedc's own ACs contain no 'depends on bd9e' or 'reuse bd9e pins' qualifier — the AC is stated as an independent deliverable of cedc
findings.finding: Both `bd9e` (AC8 + AC9) and `cedc` (AC1) independently claim to author the DC create-path `issuetype` value pins. `bd9e` states 'the type mapping is pinned by value for the DC create path, for all four local types' and declares 'this ticket owns them unconditionally'; `cedc` AC1 independently states the create-path mapper is 'pinned by VALUE for every key it emits — ... `issuetype`'. Two children will author overlapping assertions for the same observable output, creating a double-authorship conflict: if implemented in parallel the pins may diverge in form, fixture, or expected value; if implemented sequentially the second author may inadvertently override or duplicate the first without either child's AC flagging it.
scenarios: cedc is implemented before bd9e: cedc authors DC issuetype pins against the pre-unification _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE literal in jira_datacenter/backend.py; bd9e later resolves a divergence and chooses a different canonical value, silently making cedc's pins wrong without cedc's AC catching it

cedc and bd9e are implemented in parallel: two sets of DC issuetype assertions exist in different test modules with no cross-reference, possibly using different fixtures or expected values, making one set redundant or contradictory
A reviewer auditing cedc's completion sees AC1 and writes fresh pins, unaware bd9e's pins already exist, producing a duplicate corpus that will confuse future maintainers
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 'issuetype' entry from cedc AC1's enumeration and add a clause: 'issuetype pins are delivered by bd9e and referenced here; this story verifies they exist rather than re-authoring them.' Alternatively, remove bd9e AC9's DC create-path pin claim and let cedc own all characterization, with bd9e focused solely on the boundary guard and map location.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit ordering note to `cedc`'s AC1 or scope section: `cedc`'s issuetype characterization must not be authored until `bd9e` has published its canonical divergence finding; if the copies drifted, `cedc`'s expected values must match `bd9e`'s resolved canonical, not either raw copy.
evidence: bd9e AC1: 'the two existing copies are DIFFED and the result is recorded in a comment on this ticket'
bd9e AC2: 'if the two copies diverge, the chosen value is decided explicitly with its rationale recorded, not defaulted to whichever copy was moved'
cedc has no 'depends on bd9e' statement in any AC, and no qualifier that its issuetype pins should match bd9e's canonical resolution

cedc approach: 'Parametrize rather than copy ... No production change expected.' — the source of truth for issuetype values is the production code cedc's tests will characterize, but that source is being MOVED and possibly changed by bd9e
findings.finding: `cedc` has no stated ordering dependency on `bd9e`, but `cedc`'s DC create-path characterization is sensitive to the outcome of `bd9e`'s divergence investigation. `bd9e` must compare the two existing copies of `_LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE`, decide if they have drifted, and choose a canonical value. If they have drifted and `bd9e` resolves to a value that differs from what `cedc`'s independently-authored pins expect, `cedc`'s assertions will be wrong — and because neither child's ACs reference the other's resolution, the conflict is undetectable by the completion verifier.
findings.location: child cedc-58d1-f6d1-428e (AC1, overall) and child bd9e-0740-1b47-47f8 (AC1-AC2)
scenarios: The two copies have drifted on one entry (as fe15's status map had drifted by the 'deleted' key before anyone looked); bd9e resolves the canonical value to Copy A's version; cedc's pins were authored against Copy B's version; the discrepancy is silent because cedc's AC does not require agreement with bd9e's resolution
Both children are reviewed independently; the reviewer of cedc has no visibility into bd9e's divergence finding, and approves cedc's pins without knowing they may be stale
findings.suggested_fix: Add to cedc's scope or AC1: 'issuetype expected values are taken from the canonical map produced by bd9e after its divergence check; if bd9e has not yet merged, this AC is blocked.' This makes the ordering dependency explicit and prevents the silent mismatch.

findings.finding: The 79d5 plan says DC convergence tests will be 'parametrized alongside Cloud's where the mechanism is shared,' but the existing Cloud convergence suites are not structured for parametrization — they hardcode Cloud-specific internals (comment_limits.truncate_comment_body, ADF path constants, _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT) that have no DC equivalents. An implementer following the plan literally would either restructure incident-hardened Cloud tests (introducing blast radius and risk) or discover the parametrization is infeasible and fall back to separate DC files — but the plan names no fallback here, unlike cedc which explicitly says 'split is the fallback, not the default.' Without either a positive rationale for why parametrization is feasible despite these Cloud-specific internals, or an acknowledged fallback, the implementer is left to resolve this tension silently.
findings.location: 79d5-63c7-5f31-48a7 / Scope section: 'tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/ — DC convergence coverage for comment and description' and Approach step 2: 'Port both convergence suites to DC, parametrized alongside Cloud's where the mechanism is shared'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to 79d5 Scope/Approach: 'NOTE: Cloud's convergence suites hardcode Cloud-specific internals (ADF path, comment_limits module) and cannot be directly parametrized over DC without restructuring them. findings.finding: The plan's AC for `79d5` requires provenance cited 'at the `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding' in `backend.py`, but the authoritative DEFINITION site `rich_text.py:56-60` carries a comment the plan's own research explicitly identifies as wrong — it attributes the 32,767 limit to Cloud comment limits, which 'REVERSES the actual causality' (DC's limit comes from `jira.text.field.character.limit`, which governs Comments AND Description; it is not derived from Cloud's constant).
